title: Git Directory Structure
description: Map the .git directory and understand what each file and subdirectory does.

data.text: The .git directory is the home of everything Git knows about your repository. It contains your full history, all refs, hooks, config, and the object database. Understanding its layout demystifies Git's behavior and gives you a clear map for manual recovery.

data.title: Key directories and files
items: **HEAD** — Points to the current branch (symbolic ref) or commit SHA (detached).
**description** — Used by the Git daemon; not relevant for local work.
**info/** — Contains the exclude file (like .gitignore but local-only).
**objects/** — The object database (loose files + pack files).

data.title: Explore the .git directory
data.code:
# List top-level .git contents
ls -la .git/

# Show HEAD contents
cat .git/HEAD

# List all branches
tree .git/refs/heads/ -L 1

# Show all hooks
tree .git/hooks/

# Count objects
git count-objects -v

data.text: The objects directory stores all Git objects. Loose objects live directly in two-level directories (AB/CDEF...). Pack files live in objects/pack/. The packed-refs file stores refs that have been packed by git gc.
Hooks live in .git/hooks/ and are shell scripts named after the hook event. Git only runs hooks that are executable. Sample hooks with .sample extension are not executed.

data.title: Core hooks directory is not shared
data.text: The .git/hooks/ directory is not tracked by Git. To share hooks across a team, use a tool like Husky, or commit scripts and link them during setup.

items: Recover a deleted branch by reading .git/refs/heads/
Run git fsck to validate the entire object database
Check hook scripts are executable with ls -l .git/hooks/

items.question: Can I move the .git directory?
items.answer: You can change the GIT_DIR environment variable to store Git data elsewhere, but this is advanced. For normal use, keep .git at the repository root.

items.question: Is it safe to delete files in .git/objects?
items.answer: Only after running git prune or git gc. Unreachable objects are not visible to normal Git commands but still take disk space. git gc safely removes them.

items.question: What is packed-refs?
items.answer: The packed-refs file is a compact storage for refs. Git writes refs here during git gc to reduce the number of loose ref files. You can still read branches and tags normally.

items.question: Can I have a bare Git repository?
items.answer: Yes. A bare repository (created with git init --bare) has no working directory — it only contains the .git contents. Bare repos are used for shared central repositories.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: .git contains the full repository — history, refs, hooks, and config
HEAD, config, index, hooks/, objects/, and refs/ are the critical subdirectories
Objects are stored in two-level directories inside objects/
Hooks are shell scripts; must be executable to run
Bare repositories contain only Git data with no working directory
